Log"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EMay 2020\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E23rd:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EFirst day of Medicine postings, handover and briefing of the cases was done with the previous batch interns.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E24th:\u003C\/b\u003E Sunday- went for rounds with unit PG. Gave dressing for a grade 1 bedsore. Learned how to make SOAP notes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E25th:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Learned how to insert a Foley's catheter in a female patient. Observed and learned how to put Ryles tube.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E26th:\u003C\/b\u003E First OP day. An interesting case of a young male with quadriparesis was admitted. Did CNS examination and studied examination of power in mucles of the limbs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E27th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned how to take an arterial sample for ABG and venous blood sample. Learned about metabolic acidosis and treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E28th:\u003C\/b\u003E Discussion about gastroenteritis and AKI, effects of NSAIDs on kidneys.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E29th:\u003C\/b\u003E discussion of possible treatments and efficacy of treatments for AIDP. Planning next course of action for CNS patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E30th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned about nerve conduction studies and nerve biopsy. Discussion about thrombocytopenia in relation to gastroenteritis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E31st:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Sunday- read about GBS and its variants, and treatment.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EJune\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1st:\u003C\/b\u003E icu duty, discharges of patients. Learned about drugs causing thrombocytopenia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2nd:\u003C\/b\u003E amc night duty. Discussion of possible causes of severe hypokalemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3rd:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned about ECG changes and observed them in ecgs of hypokalemia patient, learned about hypokalemic periodic paralysis. Observed ascitic tap in CKD patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4th: \u003C\/b\u003ESubmitted E-log. Discussed about the efficacy of steroids in inflammatory diseases of nerves.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5th:\u003C\/b\u003E discussion about pancytopenia in HIV and necessity for bone marrow biopsy to determine cause. Monitored blood transfusion for a patient. Learned about transfusion reactions.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E6th:\u003C\/b\u003E Discussion of treatment for diabetes in a hypokalemic patient. Counseling of patient for appropriate diet in view of both conditions.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E7th:\u003C\/b\u003E First day of Nephrology duty. Monitored patients on dialysis. Learned about haemodialysis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E8th:\u003C\/b\u003E Took patient for surgery referral due to abscess formation at site of i.v. cannula. One patient developed sudden severe SOB, and saturation was rapidly falling. Patient did not respond to Oxygen supplementation, hence he was shifted to dialysis unit and bag and mask ventilation was given until saturation was raised to a sufficient level to attempt intubation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EObserved and learned Intubation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter intubation, CPAP machine was connected to the ET tube and saturation maintained. Constant monitoring was required until extubation was done.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E9th:\u003C\/b\u003E Follow up with patient who was intubated. Observed Lumbar Puncture procedure and ultrasound guided ascitic tap.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E10th:\u003C\/b\u003E First day of Psychiatry posting. Learned about SSRI, SNRIs, TCAs. Learned about schizophrenia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E11th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw a patient of General Anxiety Disorder. Learned about positive and negative symptoms.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E12th:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Learned about Dementia and depression.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E13th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about psychiatric disorders caused by metabolic disorders.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E14th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned about Dementia and Depression.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E15th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and alcohol withdrawal.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E16th:\u003C\/b\u003E Unit 2 OP duty. We had a patient presenting with severe acute chest pain since early that morning. Serial ECGs showed evolving MI. Unfortunately patient's attenders wanted to leave against medical advise. I and a co-intern had night duty. Observed procedure of establishing Central Line for a patient requiring dialysis. Learned how to obtain venous and arterial blood samples and how to give injections via IV catheter.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E17th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw a case of domestic abuse PTSD now showing dissociative disorder.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E18th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw a case of schizophrenia having 3rd person delusions, paranoia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E19th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw a case of Catatonia. Patient presented with rigidity, slow speech and decreased responsiveness. Complaints from family of hallucinations.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E20th:\u003C\/b\u003E Saw case of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. A case of Dissociative disorder presented in casuality unconscious with pseudoseizures.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E21st:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about Diuretic drugs, uses, mode of action, and side effects.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E22nd:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Learned about kidney function, specifically drugs which are nephrotoxic, effect of NSAIDs on kidneys.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E23rd:\u003C\/b\u003E OP duty. Admitted 2 patients; CVA and GE cases. Detailed history and examination was done after admission of patients. I had night duty as well. Inserted Ryles tube for ICU patient.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E24th:\u003C\/b\u003E admitted 2 emergency cases, a patient presenting with tachycardia and another patient with acute abdominal pain.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E25th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned about adenosine drug. Learned BISAP scoring for necrotizing pancreatitis. GE case patient was relieved with antibiotics and discharged.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E26th:\u003C\/b\u003E Took patient for HRCT, but it appeared the patient may have an allergic reaction to the contrast material hence patient did not consent to HRCT. Normal CT was done in which enlarged head of pancress was seen. Acute pancreatitis was suspected. 1 patient was discharged.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E27th:\u003C\/b\u003E 2 patients were relieved and discharged. Read about treatment for acute pancrestitis. Examined a case of pericardial effusion.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E28th: \u003C\/b\u003ERead about Staphylococcal aureus. Read about effects of Uremia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E29th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about heart blocks, and the ecg findings.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E30th:\u003C\/b\u003E OP day, admitted 2 patients- hypertensive emergency, secondary cushings. Emergnecy case in casuality,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EJuly\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1st:\u003C\/b\u003E Discussion about the secondary cushings patient, who seemingly developed features of cushings syndrome due to topical steroids.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2nd:\u003C\/b\u003E Hypertensive patient was taken to neurology OP for opinion regarding bilateral lower limb tingling and numbness. MRI dorsal spine was done. Observed a therapeutic pleural tap.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3rd:\u003C\/b\u003E collected reports of our patients, learned about torsades de pointes. Discussion regarding the hypertensive patient, as he had bilateral lower limb weakness and tingling sensation, which points to diagnosis other than TIA.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4th: \u003C\/b\u003EDischarged a patient. Had technical work of preparing cases with all the relative aids (videos and pictures) for the PG exams.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5th:\u003C\/b\u003E Studied about pulmonary hypertension.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E6th:\u003C\/b\u003E Studied pericardial effusion and its clinical findings and treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E7th:\u003C\/b\u003E OP day. Saw an anemia patient, heard diastolic murmur. Saw a Patient with severe limb ischemia, so much pain that he required morphine, which is not available in our hospital. Hypoglycemia patient and a heart failure patient were admitted.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E8th:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Took patient for orthopedics referral due to complaints of knee pain. They requested xray, so took patient for xray. The patient had tall T-waves on ecg, and slightky elevated potassium levels, hence 2D-echo was done, but no abnormalities were found.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E9th:\u003C\/b\u003E patient was taken to cect, with bowel preparation done.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E10th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about heart failure, and different types of pulses seen in heart failure.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E11th:\u003C\/b\u003E Took patient for chest xray and reporting of xray.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E12th:\u003C\/b\u003E read about pneumonia, how to diagnose and xray findings, treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E13th:\u003C\/b\u003E collected CT report of patient. Learned about Shone complex and treatment of heart failure.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E14th:\u003C\/b\u003E OP day. Very dull as patients were few, and unwilling to get admitted.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E15th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned about Circle of Willis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E16th:\u003C\/b\u003E Learned the areas of brain and how to locate effected areas based on symptoms.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E17th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about Uremic Encephalopathy in CKD patients.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E18th:\u003C\/b\u003E Discussed about Malaria, and the differences between textbook findings and in reality presentation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E19th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about Cholera and mechanism of action of its toxin in causing diarrhea.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E20th:\u003C\/b\u003E Read about Dengue and other causes of platelet deficiencies.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E21st:\u003C\/b\u003E OP day. Admitted 5 patients. One pancreatitis, heart failure, dengue suspect, and CVA case. One was a returning patient with CIDP.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E22nd:\u003C\/b\u003E Last day of Medicine postings. Took pancreatitis patient for CECT. Report confirmed acute pancreatitis. Briefed the next batch interns of the cases in our unit.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/6380714525530987624\/posts\/default\/3830114112513742555"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/6380714525530987624\/posts\/default\/3830114112513742555"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/pri422.blogspot.com\/2020\/06\/daily-log.html","title":"Daily Log"}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"Priyanka Vaddi"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/07566904918407048356"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}]},{"id":{"$t":"tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-6380714525530987624.post-6742434067796677234"},"published":{"$t":"2020-06-02T12:14:00.000-07:00"},"updated":{"$t":"2020-07-02T17:48:54.822-07:00"},"title":{"type":"text","$t":"Medicine Intern Log"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"Hello everyone, I am a medical intern, and recently started my Medicine posting. This blog is to share my experience and the cases I come across during this period.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his guardian's signed informed consent.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHere we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003ECASE\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAn 18 year old male patient came with complaints of tingling and numbness of both feet since 15 days, and both hands since 6 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\nPatient was apparently asymptomatic 15 days back, then when he had gone out to wash his feet, he noticed he could not feel the sensation of water flow. It was sudden in onset and gradually progressed up to the knee joint bilaterally. Followed by edema of both feet which was sudden in onset and gradually progressive, and increased on walking, and decreased on rest. Edema then subsided after 3 days without medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGradually he had difficulty wearing chappal since 10 days, which progressed to difficulty in climbing the stairs since 8 days, and difficulty squatting since 6 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\nLater upper limbs also became involved, with an electric shock like sensation in both hands, distal muscle hand weakness since 5 days, and proximal hand weakness since 5 days. It was gradually progressive, and strength improved since 2 days. At the time he presented to the hospital, he was unable to walk or stand without support, unable to eat by himself, button his shirt, or comb his hair.\u003Cbr\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\nNeck muscle is normal\u003Cbr\u003E\nRolling over on bed is normal\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo h\/o breathing difficulty\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo diurnal variations\u003Cbr\u003E\nLimbs are flaccid and loose\u003Cbr\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo wasting\/ thinning of muscle\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo h\/o pain, fatigue, muscle cramps, fasciculations, twitching of muscles, or involuntary movements.\u003Cbr\u003E\nHe is able to feel cloth\u003Cbr\u003E\nAble to differentiate hot and cold water\u003Cbr\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\nHe is having numbness, and sense of walking on cotton wool\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo root pain, neck pain, back pain or band-like sensation.\u003Cbr\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo h\/o vomiting, fever, loose stools, diarrhoea, sore throat, cough, chest pain, loss of consciousness, speech disturbances, delusions, or hallucinations.\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo giddiness or palpitations.\u003Cbr\u003E\nBowel and bladder intact.\u003Cbr\u003E\nno h\/o DM, HTN, Epilepsy, CVA, TB, Thyroid\u003Cbr\u003E\nSleep is normal.\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo h\/o smoking or alcohol intake.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\nGeneral examination:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\nPatient is c\/c\/c and oriented.\u003Cbr\u003E\nModerately built and nourished\u003Cbr\u003E\nPallor- absent\u003Cbr\u003E\nIcterus -absent \u003Cbr\u003E\nNo cyanosis, clubbing, lymphadenopathy \u003Cbr\u003E\nTemp- afebrile\u003Cbr\u003E\nBP: 100\/70 mm hg\u003Cbr\u003E\nPR: 54 bpm\u003Cbr\u003E\nCVS: s1 s2 heard, no murmurs\u003Cbr\u003E\nRS: BAE+ NVBS\u003Cbr\u003E\nP\/A: soft, non tender\u003Cbr\u003E\n\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\nCNS\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003Cbr\u003E\nSpeech: normal\u003Cbr\u003E\nCranial nerves , He became able to walk slowly without support. His RR did not increase, suggesting respiratory muscles are also intact.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003EVidoe of his gait:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/drive.google.com\/file\/d\/1ruI_SlpMZ9uI-PDWd_odX7-rK6ULlBr8\/view?usp=sharing\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/drive.google.com\/file\/d\/1ruI_SlpMZ9uI-PDWd_odX7-rK6ULlBr8\/view?usp=sharing\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; We know that the pathology is in the nerves, specifically the peripheral nerves, but it is not clear which part of the nerve is involved (axon\/ myelin sheath), or to what extent.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan\u003EThe patient was sent for Nerve Conduction Studies to learn a little more about his condition.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient's NCS:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/drive.google.com\/file\/d\/1sL3r2ufPInzv7hrDAMr4TieOe_cHlBw9\/view?usp=sharing\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/drive.google.com\/file\/d\/1sL3r2ufPInzv7hrDAMr4TieOe_cHlBw9\/view?usp=sharing\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe study was done, but came as not recordable, which suggested severe axonal damage.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe report suggested Acute motor and sensory axonal neuropathy.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh2-VKYNGxiGTGWu1C1Ce4-bGv9V2Uw1qestPMa9ztZVokvr-bAYZcxD0dcAwgw7ghvDmq5PU06U4n3YeCbZ6gGElMtavRg6NRwl66Hloh0ewcmBYw7Ie7mIX5YewPL8NyNPNlHKPvSVd_P\/s1600\/1591128693623813-0.png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh2-VKYNGxiGTGWu1C1Ce4-bGv9V2Uw1qestPMa9ztZVokvr-bAYZcxD0dcAwgw7ghvDmq5PU06U4n3YeCbZ6gGElMtavRg6NRwl66Hloh0ewcmBYw7Ie7mIX5YewPL8NyNPNlHKPvSVd_P\/s1600\/1591128693623813-0.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh0aTYf261-UwSk88rhwjDFxoR_5oUdtkQFK5cE-Y9buyFGDjiqwBmWH9rff3mr09h1WaQ-Z8C-nK_PZGrvd8jhlEUJSL8wIWaM3ghyIWmjOwviY-ZFmsaoiUhhFEZlZqNRSdRiHtRBeyUx\/s1600\/1591128689175015-1.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EWe contemplated a nerve biopsy next, but as it would not effect the treatment, and thus an unnecessary expense, it was not done.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdvice at discharge:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. Physiotherapy of all 4 limbs\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. Tab. B-complex OD\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMajority of patients with GBS gradually improve on their own to a large extent if not fully. As this patient is already showing some improvement, we have hope that he will have a good recovery.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFollow up after 2 weeks:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient showed slight improvement in hand muscles. Gait and power also showed improvement.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/6380714525530987624\/posts\/default\/6742434067796677234"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/6380714525530987624\/posts\/default\/6742434067796677234"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/pri422.blogspot.com\/2020\/06\/medicine-intern-log.html","title":"Medicine
